evals.prompt: I just finished building a ProductCard organism for our Design System. It uses DSImage, DSText, DSBadge atoms, and has variants (compact/expanded) and states (default/loading/empty). I need to write the README. What sections are required and what should I include?
evals.expected_output: Lists all 9 required sections: Title, Usage (compiling example), API table, Enums, Tokens, Composition tree, States, Figma URL, Anti-patterns. Notes organisms always require README. Provides structure/template guidance.

assertions.text: Response lists all 9 required README sections: Title, Usage, API, Enums, Tokens, Composition, States, Figma, Anti-patterns
Response states that organisms ALWAYS require a README
Response emphasizes the Usage section must include a functional code example that compiles

evals.prompt: Do I need to write a README for every atom in the Design System? What about molecules?
evals.expected_output: Atoms normally don't need a separate README. Molecules need one only if composition logic is non-obvious. Organisms always need one. Distinguishes between inline code comments (not mandatory) and separate README docs.

assertions.text: Response states atoms normally do NOT require a separate README
Response states molecules need README only when composition logic is non-obvious
Response states organisms ALWAYS need a README
